reviews.text: The poor visual effects, questionable stylistic choices, and a dragging story with a poor script distract you from the good aspects the film has.
reviews.author: Hector A. Gonzalez

reviews.text: At best, Jungle Cruise is mildly entertaining, with traces of a better film peppered throughout. At worst, it reminds you that Pirates of the Caribbean did all this way better twenty years ago, and nothing seems to have progressed since.
reviews.author: Joonatan Itkonen

reviews.text: I think we would all agree to hop in a boat with these two as they take us on an adventure.
reviews.author: Jillian Chilingerian

reviews.text: The SUMMER ADVENTURE you all need to go on! With vibes from Raiders of the Lost Ark to Pirates of the Caribbean! this movie will bring a smile to your face the entire cruise.
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: Sometimes movies should exist to be entertainment, purely and simply. Jungle Cruise should have been that, and it’s a shame there was not enough charisma to keep it afloat.
reviews.author: Tina Kakadelis

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise is exactly what it makes itself out to be: a big-name summer blockbuster...
reviews.author: Annie Banks

reviews.text: A family adventure through familiar, albeit shallow, waters.
reviews.author: Benjamin Wiebe

reviews.text: Any minor quibbles are outshone by the star power wattage generated by Johnson and Blunt. If Johnson is still the Most Electrifying Man In Entertainment, then Emily Blunt is a superconductor.
reviews.author: Dallas King

reviews.text: Book your trip on Jungle Cruise now. It’s a first-class ticket.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: JUNGLE CRUISE (the movie) was based on "Jungle Cruise", a Disneyland ride, so I wasn't expecting much, and was definitely pleasantly surprised. All in all, this is a fun movie.
reviews.author: Mark R. Leeper

reviews.text: The script (from the trio of Michael Green, Glenn Ficarra and John Requa) is silly and light-hearted, reminiscent of the late-1960’s pulp you would find at a Saturday afternoon matinee.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Inspired, too inspired, on its titular Disney attraction ride. Dwayne Johnson is practically the attraction's tour guide. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise manages to coast on the charm of its two leads, making it a fun, if somewhat forgettable, adventure.
reviews.author: Daniel Howat

reviews.text: JUNGLE CRUISE is a really enjoyable retro action-adventure film for the entire family, that shines with its great stars, wonderful chemistry and a surprisingly good and always entertaining story.
reviews.author: Jimmy Cage

reviews.text: Despite the flaws, theres something about Jungle Cruise that just works. Its a traditional summer blockbuster that combines charming leads with enough adventure to keep everyone happy.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: Unlike the vast majority of other recent Disney Live-Action features, Jungle Cruise is a film easy to have a good time with.
reviews.author: Carson Timar

reviews.text: If theres a ride that the Jungle Cruise feels more like than the Jungle Cruise, its Pirates of the Caribbean. And sadly, I have to say that this is this movies biggest downfall.
reviews.author: Mat Brunet

reviews.text: No amount of money, not even the reported 200 million budget, can help Jungle Cruise avoid tasting like a hunk of processed meat from the Disney conveyor belt.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise is passable light-hearted family entertainment.
reviews.author: Jeff Nelson

reviews.text: As far as these things go, this one isn't half-bad, and that's almost entirely due to the presence of Dwayne Johnson and Emily Blunt.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: Successfully brings a beloved Disneyland ride to life.
reviews.author: Kate Robertson

reviews.text: The scenery is beautiful and it is a fun ride along with Emily Blunt and Dwayne Johnson but it is no African Queen.
reviews.author: Julia Swift

reviews.text: Disney has an unlimited supply of backlog intellectual properties they can recycle/reimagine/reconfigure forever. These titles make money and win-over unknowing new audiences, but in the end, it's filmmaking at its most safe, lazy, and unimaginative.
reviews.author: Michael Clark

reviews.text: Without the jolly fun of watching Blunt and Johnson wriggle out of tough situations and give some spark to their green-screen acting, the slick Jungle Cruise would be just another visual effects-heavy escapade that we have seen many times before.
reviews.author: Lynn Venhaus

reviews.text: Full of Indiana Jones and Sunday comic strips humor, but with Disney DNA. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fausto Fernandez

reviews.text: As slick as they come, and just as generic. Even the leads' charm feels pre-polished.
reviews.author: Witney Seibold

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise is by no means a perfect movie. It has a few flaws that stop me from giving a wholehearted recommendation. But it is a fun, campy movie you can enjoy with the family, and a diverting throwback to the 80s and 90s adventure films.
reviews.author: Kshitij Rawat

reviews.text: This Amazon adventure veers off course...
reviews.author: Udita Jhunjhunwala

reviews.text: An unapologetic archeological swashbuckler...[and] a movie that bites off perhaps a bit more than it can chew.
reviews.author: Luke Parker

reviews.text: The Pirates of the Caribbean hangover is so strong with Jungle Cruise that it almost makes you wonder if Dwayne Johnson swiped Captain Jack Sparrow's stash of rum and had himself a jolly old time before filming.
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise is not short on ambition and chemistry between the two leads. But ... the action simply doesn't pop in any new or exciting way most of the time.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise is a fun cinematic ride that will certainly set pulses racing, but its lack of originality and reliance on CGI and narrative tropes leaves it feeling like we've seen this all somewhere else before.
reviews.author: Ben Turner

reviews.text: Collett-Serra mechanically serves up stingy doses of action, humor and romance -- watching his film is like watching an alien try to create a summer blockbuster based on a checklist.
reviews.author: Bennett Campbell Ferguson

reviews.text: Little added touches like Jesse Plemmons' strange Bavarian accent and whatever Paul Giamatti was going for in the film elevates JUNGLE CRUISE from eye-rolling to good.
reviews.author: James Clay

reviews.text: Instead of hitting those racing rapids with excitement, you're left feeling a little jaded and just a bit damp when the thrills never quite emerge.
reviews.author: Zehra Phelan

reviews.text: Let's hope the next time Disney puts a portion of their theme park on the big screen they use half as many writers, and keep things more on the rails.
reviews.author: Taylor Baker

reviews.text: So crass and phony that it can make the sincere adventure seeker feel had.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: Despite the best intentions, it comes across as a very unadventurous adventure.
reviews.author: Matthew Toomey

reviews.text: [Jaume Collet-Serra's] a really good director and you can tell how much fun he's having with this.
reviews.author: Kristian Harloff

reviews.text: If you've been missing The Pirates of the Caribbean franchise, Jungle Cruise is here to tide you over until a planned sixth film in that profitable but often-incoherent action-adventure-comedy arrives.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: Dwayne Johnson and Emily Blunt make this a Jungle Cruise you'll want to book.
reviews.author: Dirk Libbey

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise is harmless fun, kept afloat by the watchability factor of its three leads and a relentless, lively pace that means it's never boring and never a chore. But it's also not even remotely exceptional.
reviews.author: Paul Mount

reviews.text: It gets zero points for originality, but it's fun.
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: It tries its best to be fun, and it sometimes succeeds, but not quite often enough to escape the creeping feeling that this action-packed, fast-paced jungle adventure is actually...a little tedious.
reviews.author: Audrey Fox

reviews.text: The general sexlessness of the Disney machine can make even the most chaste underwater exchanges of oxygen look downright heated. Just imagine if any of the sorta-flirtatious patter had the zing of a screwball pairing!
reviews.author: Jesse Hassenger

reviews.text: As is too often the case with Disney's bigger films it's a product made by committee, but happily, it at least gives the appearance of something and some place new.
reviews.author: Rob Hunter

reviews.text: It borrows so much from other properties that it fails to create its own identity.
reviews.author: Rosa Parra

reviews.text: An example of the venerable genre of the jungle adventure film, it is not well written, but it is fun, in an easygoing, campy kind of way.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: Being fun but weightless and wildly derivative might be forgivable if they had hired even one female department head. Disney should do better representing 51% of the world below the line.
reviews.author: Leslie Combemale

reviews.text: Johnson is his usual lovable self, but the way his story unfolds is hard to swallow.
reviews.author: Ja-Quan Greene

reviews.text: For the most part, every set piece is run-of-the-mill, the stakes are mild at best and the whole thing goes on for way too long. There's not much chemistry between Blunt and The Rock, although both are good sports.
reviews.author: Jorge Ignacio Castillo

reviews.text: Indiana Jones meets Lara Croft is the obvious, and largely accurate, shorthand, but with a richer seam of humour, the jeopardy laced with a healthy helping of jokes.
reviews.author: Terry Staunton

reviews.text: Starts out great but about halfway through it goes totally off the rails.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: A delightful amalgam of Pirates of the Caribbean, The Mummy (1999), Johnson's Jumanji series, and other entertaining adventure films.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: Delivers some fun and plenty of silliness, if by treading lightly across the action-adventure-scape of gone-by classics.
reviews.author: Bill Arceneaux

reviews.text: An entertaining, though unimaginative, family saga that banks on the charisma of its leading couple and its old-fashioned formula. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: The real race in "Jungle Cruise" is to if see you lose track of or lose interest in the plot first.
reviews.author: Neil Morris

reviews.text: The movie is in constant motion, like a giant roller coaster ride of Jungle Cruise, Grizzly River Run and WaterWorld show rolled into one. Jungle Cruise is an entertaining escapist for the whole family.
reviews.author: Nathalia Aryani

reviews.text: It feels that he and the screenwriters were so obsessed with the visuals that they simply forgot the human emotions. This adventure has no soul.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: Sailing very familiar waters, Jungle Cruise is predictable family fare but also rather fun, and its action sequences sweetly thrilling.
reviews.author: Sarah Cartland

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise is exactly what you expect it to be, a bombastic but bland action-adventure jam packed with outlandish set pieces, clocking in at 30 minutes too long.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: It's great fun, high-action and doesn't take itself too seriously.
reviews.author: Aine O'Connor

reviews.text: [F]or those who like popcorn-munching adventure fare, you could do worse, particularly when you have a central pairing like The Rock and Emily Blunt bantering and brawling their way through the film's center. It's fun, and sometimes, that's all you need.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: A big-budget romp working itself into a tizzy without succeeding in shaking the feeling of déjà-vu that it engenders.
reviews.author: Andrea Chase

reviews.text: The film's playful cheerfulness is the very thing that prevents its rough first act from sinking this ship altogether.
reviews.author: Rubén Rosario

reviews.text: For an hour it is the passable version of much greater and just average adventures until it leans hard into special effects leaving us with a less exciting and far less fun version of the initial Pirates of the Caribbean films.
reviews.author: Erik Childress

reviews.text: [Blunt is] so much better than anything else in the movie that she makes it not only tolerable but sometimes surprisingly enjoyable.
reviews.author: Mark Feeney

reviews.text: [Jungle Cruise] isn't as thrilling as it should be.
reviews.author: Allyson Johnson

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise is pretty boring, mostly unpleasant to watch, and seems to be a gigantic waste of time and money, all of which it honestly pains me to say to you.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: A summer blockbuster that sails on the fizzy chemistry between Dwayne Johnson and Emily Blunt.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: It's hard to make colonization a cheery good time, but Jungle Cruise tries.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise is Disney very much trying to do the Pirates of the Caribbean thing, and when the movie manages to nail its tone, it works very well and is extremely entertaining. However, the moments when it doesn't work, it feels very redundant.
reviews.author: Kaitlyn Booth

reviews.text: A daft and daring adventure ready to sweep you along for the ridiculous ride - if you let it.
reviews.author: Tori Brazier

reviews.text: Highlights such as a smashing prelude in London, a delightful chemistry between Lily and Captain Frank help keep our attention.
reviews.author: Wendy Shreve

reviews.text: You've been on the ride before, but twenty minutes in, you're thinking this is fun...scrappy with a 70s feel, good fun and it does what it says on the tin.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: Despite the obvious chemistry between Johnson and Blunt, along the way its jungle adventure becomes dull and gets lost like a canoe on the river as it follows the map of Disney's well-known formulas to the letter. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: This Jungle Cruise is a pure summertime crowd-pleaser.
reviews.author: Mike Scott

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise joins the select - but interesting - list of films whose genesis lies in the heart of Disneyland and manages to inject us with a good dose of adrenaline on screen. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Arturo Magaña

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise never achieves the heights of movies like Pirates of the Caribbean...it's still a fun ride due to Blunt and Johnson's chemistry and performances.
reviews.author: Nicole Ackman

reviews.text: While the story is formulaic in terms of typical action-adventure tales, it really does shine with the chemistry between its leads.
reviews.author: Britany Murphy

reviews.text: The best Disney ride movie since Pirates of the Caribbean- pure good clean fun with a surprising supernatural twist and puns...plenty of puns.
reviews.author: Lisa Johnson Mandell

reviews.text: Plays well on established properties like  Raiders of the Lost Ark,  The Mummy  , and even Disney's own  Pirates of the Caribbean to create an agreeable mix of comedy and swashbuckling action.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: Ultimately, Jungle Cruise is just not good enough to make viewers ever forget this is a film designed to bring Disney fans back to the parks.
reviews.author: Ani Bundel

reviews.text: It's something closer to an amusement-park attraction named Generic Blockbuster Cruise, where you slowly glide past a bunch of prefab set-ups and the whole thing moves inexorably forward on a track, while a skipper cracks the same corny jokes.
reviews.author: David Fear

reviews.text: It's well worth buying a ticket on this river ride. There's action, there's romance and, if you like puns, plenty of comedy. You might even come up with puns of your own, realizing that it's set on a giant Amazon stream that's not streaming on Amazon.
reviews.author: Jason Fraley

reviews.text: Though Jungle Cruise has moments of trashy fun (such as Plemons's goofy performance), this particular film overall is smoothed out in service of broad Disney accessibility.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise is not aiming to sweep the Academy Awards... But anything involving underwater chambers where Emily Blunt has to kiss Dwayne Johnson for oxygen can be enjoyed for its sheer escapism.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: Unfortunately, the film declines markedly towards the end, although it does try to show off there. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: It's too long and it moves at an erratic pace - sometimes hyperactively - but it's easily digestible, while occasionally problematic. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: ... plays like a fantastic tale fit for toddlers fleshed out with sequences giving those same children nightmares... any goodwill the film earns is squandered in dropped story threads and plot execution.
reviews.author: Kevin A. Ranson

reviews.text: For the most part, the movie's two luminous stars share just enough wattage to light the screen with cheeky banter and faint touches of a potentially sizzling romance.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise is escapism through and through.
reviews.author: Michael Ward

reviews.text: Collet-Serra creates a romp of a picture booby-trapped with adventure movie tropes (arcane curses, snakes, evil Germans) which, while they might seem familiar to Indiana Jones fans, still combine to make for a decent family flick.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: Blunt is her usual brisk, honeyed self, but Johnson plays comedy like he's doing power lifts.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: Enjoyable nonsense that surprisingly wastes little time. It gives movie goers exactly what they'd want to see out of Jungle film starring Dwayne Johnson and Emily Blunt.
reviews.author: Doug Walker

reviews.text: [Jungle Cruise's] flaws aren't entirely the fault of the Disney approach: Johnson can do a lot of things, but playing a human being struggling with romantic feelings isn't one of them.
reviews.author: Anthony Morris

reviews.text: This doesn't lead to anything particularly interesting, but... large parts of the first half are, in fact, actively charming.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: Feels not just designed by committee, but by a corporation... like every theme park ride, the film's modest pleasures fade oh-so-quickly afterwards.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: Emily Blunt and Dwayne Johnson are hilarious and their chemistry is insane. However, it's not enough to save this high on action low on substance fantasy, action adventure
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: There are plenty of laughs, vibrant images, and escapist fun for the whole family. This could easily be Disney's next franchise.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: A bit bloated for a movie based on a theme park ride, but overall entertaining enough for the whole family, though a bit scary for really young kids. Dwayne Johnson + Emily Blunt made for a fun duo, but it's Jesse Plemons who easily stole the movie!
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise is light-hearted fun that the whole family can enjoy. It's full of exciting set-pieces, over-the-top performances, and supernatural thrills.
reviews.author: Victor Stiff

reviews.text: Is it a good time with a good crew? Well, it might not be the most wild ride in the world, but it's definitely worth the ticket.
reviews.author: Johnny Gayzmonic

reviews.text: It's the performances by Johnson and Blunt and the evolving chemistry between their characters that makes the film work.
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: There may be nobody on the Hollywood casting speed-dial capable of doing the heavy lifting on a whole lot of nothing like Dwayne Johnson.
reviews.author: Jim Slotek

reviews.text: A welcome throwback to the family adventure movies of the 80s and 90s, and easily the best attempt by Disney to emulate Pirates of the Caribbean's success yet.
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: ...while the result is well-upholstered, it's also as generic and uninspired as the title...
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: The mesmerizing mayhem of this riverboat journey is a delightful throwback for fans of the old-school adventure genre with chemistry that practically jumps through the screen.
reviews.author: Alicia Gilstorf

reviews.text: The two leads are a majority of the draw and nearly one hundred percent the reason Jungle Cruise makes it to its destination, sputtering in a wonky boat on an unconventional mission.
reviews.author: Candice McMillan

reviews.text: As its cat-and-mouse plot becomes waterlogged by supernatural twists, and the contrived peril morphs the film into another action-hero vehicle for Dwayne Johnson, the emotional stakes remain docked.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: Emily Blunt and Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson drip with charismatic energy throughout the two hour runtime.
reviews.author: Valerie Complex

reviews.text: It is far from cringe or embarrassment, and sure, it's never actively terrible. But the bar shouldn't be set this low. This is a Disney adventure blockbuster led by Emily Blunt and Dwayne Johnson. We should've gotten something better than this.
reviews.author: Kevin L. Lee

reviews.text: Thanks to its stars, "Jungle Cruise" is a pleasantly forgettable voyage.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: While Whitehall lands his laughs (and gets a surprise scene for a Disney film), he can't distract from the Kathleen Turner/Michael Douglas vibes Blunt and Johnson emit. They work well together, even though they're walking in others' shoes.
reviews.author: Bruce R. Miller

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise runs too long at a little over two hours and it doesn't help when the story is nothing more than a generic action-adventure that shamelessly rips off from other like-minded genre films.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise is just plain, good, not-to-be-taken-seriously fun.
reviews.author: Alan Ng

reviews.text: Johnson and Blunt hit all the right notes to keep Jungle Cruise funny and sweep you along, but it's Whitehall's character that keeps the story feeling fresh and less predictable.
reviews.author: Rick Marshall

reviews.text: I'm impressed that it wasn't dumb. It's just energetic; I think Dwayne 'The Rock' Johnson and Emily Blunt have an okay chemistry... But Blunt here is great.
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise is a rollicking, rollercoaster of an adventure in the classic Disney style...get to your local theater and take this ride.
reviews.author: Damond Fudge

reviews.text: It's a lot of fun. It's got the adventure, it's got the action, it's got the humor... Dwayne Johnson and Emily Blunt have a great chemistry together.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: The chemistry between Blunt and Johnson, plus the right level of thrills, are enough to make entertaining an otherwise predictable and previously visited story
reviews.author: J. Don Birnam

reviews.text: It's so jam-packed with good feelings, fantastic puns, and popcorn-flavored action that you'll likely make it an annual viewing tradition.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise cribs from the Indy playbook early and often, and what begins as respectful nods to Raiders of the Lost Ark etc soon descends to shameless appropriation.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: If you can imagine Dwayne Johnson, the artist formerly known as The Rock, filling in for Johnny Depp's Captain Jack Sparrow in the "Pirates of the Caribbean" movies, you have a pretty solid idea of how Disney's "Jungle Cruise" is going to go.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: No surprise if waves of material seem reminiscent of "Pirates of the Caribbean" rolling down the Amazon. Actually, the real "Cruise" gets a courtesy salute early on when a punny -- not to be confused with funny -- Dwayne Johnson is introduced as skipper.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: Jaume Collet-Serra does his best to inject some weird electricity into Jungle Cruise, but even a B-movie virtuoso like him can get swallowed up in Disney's waters...
reviews.author: Adam Nayman

reviews.text: In a moviemaking era dominated by other properties...it feels increasingly likely that any theme park film adaptation that isn't the Pirates of the Caribbean will walk the plank.
reviews.author: Miles Surrey

reviews.text: So Jungle Cruise is lumpy and inconsistent in pace, just like many other heavily calculated, very expensive Disney junk-art products that one is somewhat loathe to admit that one somewhat enjoyed.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: If you are in lockdown and seeking a few hours of light relief, this 128-minute film, available on Disney+, should do the trick.
reviews.author: Stephen Romei

reviews.text: The studio's been working on a Jungle Cruise movie for a decade and a half, and this film is a decent enough adventure picture until it gets bogged down in elaborate mythology and CGI.
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: The movie hits some doldrums, but when the engine works, it's smooth cruising.
reviews.author: Petrana Radulovic

reviews.text: Despite an overload of subplots, CGI and bad jokes, Disney's Emily Blunt-Dwayne Johnson adventure movie seldom satisfies.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Nothing matters in Jungle Cruise.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: If the absurd, supernatural action-thriller comedy Jungle Cruise doesn't qualify as a disastrous waste of acting talents, it certainly underutilizes them.
reviews.author: Dann Gire

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise is actually a mash-up of Indiana Jones and Pirates of the Caribbean. It borrows a bit from each film and puts the phrase "steal from the best" to good use.
reviews.author: Courtney Lanning

reviews.text: Acting in franchise blockbusters often amounts to get-the-job-done professionalism. In Jungle Cruise, however, the actors approach the material as if they're enjoying a day out at Disneyland.
reviews.author: Stephen Humphries

reviews.text: I wouldn't say Jungle Cruise gives fun a bad name, but the characters and story are strictly off-the-rack.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise is a swash-buckling summer blockbuster, reminiscent of adventure romances like The Mummy and Romancing The Stone, that is fun for the whole family.
reviews.author: Lauren Bradshaw

reviews.text: Big dumb fun as Dwayne Johnson continues his family-friendly adventure film career.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: Original it ain't, neither subtle nor clever in its cock-eyed re-concoctions. You've been on this ride before.
reviews.author: Stephen Garrett

reviews.text: Like a much better version of the Pirates Of The Caribbean movies, which were very bad. Is that what we wanted? Is this what we want?
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: Gets by mostly on the charisma of its stars, an impressive production design, and one of the year's best villain performances
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: You might sit through 10 instances of Frank's river-themed wordplay, hoping one of them would make you laugh, only to find that no pun in ten did.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: Like the famed Disneyland ride that inspired it, Jungle Cruise is jammed with instantly forgettable silliness; moreover the whole thing is 100 percent synthetic.
reviews.author: Robert W. Butler

reviews.text: If you have kids, I think they'll probably really enjoy themselves.
reviews.author: Jeremy Jahns

reviews.text: While the movie does rush off in too many storytelling directions in a very cluttered second half, it never stops being entertaining for a heartbeat.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise so blatantly borrows from other movies that, yes, it suffers by not equaling any of them. But as its own thing, for current audiences who may not even get the old references, it's a fine, fun romp
reviews.author: Luke Y. Thompson

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise feels like a movie based on a 1955 theme park ride, with too many cooks in the writers' room yet not enough tar to plug its many plot holes.
reviews.author: Hanna Flint

reviews.text: A slick, family-friendly adventure set in 1916 that shamelessly fuses Raiders Of The Lost Ark with The African Queen...
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: It's not Pirates of the Caribbean, the original ride film, a Harrison Ford adventure or The African Queen, but it's what we have now.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: "...packed with actors who are essentially charm machines, churning out watchable moments as fast as the camera can capture them...it's through that magic that Jungle Cruise rises above its shortcomings to become an enjoyable popcorn movie ride."
reviews.author: Matthew Jackson

reviews.text: This movie starts well enough, then slowly veers off the rails before becoming something else entirely, all the while missing out on easy, fun opportunities to make the most of its setting.
reviews.author: Abby Olcese

reviews.text: What could have been a fun, old-fashioned family adventure is nothing but a big summer bummer.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: In what appears to be Disney's quest to make every ride a standalone film, Jungle Cruise proves to be on the higher end of the successful adaptation scale -- with a big assist from its two leads.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: Not offensive enough to be seen as a soulless cash grab but not good enough to make you feel that your time is being valued, Jungle Cruise is a misfire.
reviews.author: Terence Johnson

reviews.text: To bulk up the thin material, the film steals from countless other, better adventure movies to create an altogether less satisfying combo plate that costs $30 to rent on Disney+.
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise has nothing original to offer. We get essentially the same story as Pirate's of the Caribbean with slightly different window dressing.
reviews.author: Megan Basham

reviews.text: The picture might have amounted to something had it been able to deliver on the one essential element any kind of adventure (even one made primarily for kids) needs: a real sense of danger.
reviews.author: Bilge Ebiri

reviews.text: Despite some flaws in pacing and grotesque images, it's still fun family fare. And you don't have to wait an hour and a half in line for a dose of adventure.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: Gleeful swashbuckling fun.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: An amusing, if also blander version of Pirates of the Caribbean and Raiders of the Lost Ark with leads lacking chemistry.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: ... This movie manages about what's expected of a film version of a goofy amusement park boat ride: It's a pleasant distraction, and is just as likely to float in through one ear and then sail right on out through the other.
reviews.author: Allison Shoemaker

reviews.text: "Jungle Cruise" is more "Night at the Museum" than "African Queen." This approach will work for some, but I found it to be a frustrating missed opportunity.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: Could have been a fun Indiana Jones-style adventure, but instead is an over-long, CGI/green screen slog that recycles almost all the bad jokes/puns skippers use on the Magic Kingdom ride within the movie's first 15 minutes.
reviews.author: Rob Owen

reviews.text: Dwayne Johnson and Emily Blunt elevate Jungle Cruise, but you've seen this movie before, and you've seen it done a lot better.
reviews.author: Scott Campbell

reviews.text: Rock & Blunt create a AFRICAN-QUEEN-meets-Indiana Jones trip, apropos to a film based on a theme park ride. Love Whitehall's comic relief, part of the fun and humor. Rock on!
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: The Dwayne Johnson-Emily Blunt vehicle a charming, low-key family adventure film that strives and mostly succeeds in making a politically correct journey down the Amazon.
reviews.author: Jana Monji

reviews.text: Wonderfully escapist, dripping with magnificently congenial charm thanks to the comic chemistry of Dwayne Johnson and Emily Blunt. Plus it's sure to enrage people who use 'woke' as an insult. Yay!
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: Sometimes it's ok to turn off our cynical sides and enjoy pure escapism.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: Full of color, puns, a roaring hippopotamus and the backside of water. Between the script and the actors, it delivers an "I can't stop myself from laughing" kind of laugh.
reviews.author: Brigid Presecky

reviews.text: It's a moldy Indiana Jones knockoff clumsily sutured onto a rotting Pirates of the Caribbean knockoff.
reviews.author: Daniel Barnes

reviews.text: It is also a film carried almost entirely on the back of the charm of its stars.
reviews.author: Matthew Razak

reviews.text: While there is some fun to be had, Jungle Cruise lacks the magic of the franchise it wants to be.
reviews.author: Kevin Brackett

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise is as airy and inert as the static mannequins that fill the actual theme park attraction.
reviews.author: Drew Dietsch

reviews.text: When the world of a movie seems so palpably fake, it's hard for the people or the stakes to feel real.
reviews.author: Matt Singer

reviews.text: The Rock and Emily Blunt knock themselves out to entertain in this dopey, derivative, theme-park ride of a movie. But, hey, the kids will love it and like the Metallica thrasher that bizarrely shows up on the soundtrack, "nothing else matters."
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: I didn't have any fun, and there's really not anything more to say.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: A lot of the movie relies on Blunt and Johnson's chemistry and charm, which certainly helps elevate the movie. The pair bounce off each other with ease, developing a quick rapport that jumps from comedic to romantic to dramatic when needed.
reviews.author: Brandon Zachary

reviews.text: It is a fine adventure with two genuine movie stars that may very well become a rewatchable staple like the films it references. But on first watch, it mostly comes across as an earnest and safe homage.
reviews.author: Lindsey Bahr

reviews.text: Dwayne Johnson may not be the world's most nuanced actor, but he's a marvelous showman. His and co-star Emily Blunt's combined "it" factor transcends the sillier stretches of this somewhat forgettable but still chuckling good-times ride.
reviews.author: Kimberley Jones

reviews.text: My low tolerance for Jungle Cruise is because they had all the ingredients. This really could have been pretty good! It was like a runner with a big lead. All the runner has to do is not fall. Just finish the race and you'll win.
reviews.author: Mike Ryan

reviews.text: Finally, a movie exhausted parents everywhere can watch again and again and still enjoy.
reviews.author: Chelsea Steiner

reviews.text: An enjoyably chaotic romp which feels both fresh and yet familiar.
reviews.author: Linda Marric

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise is an example of very good commercial cinema. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: Thanks to the cast's charisma, Jungle Cruise successfully revisits a genre already forgotten by Hollywood, which, thanks to this new adventure, could resurface. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rolando Gallego

reviews.text: In between the weightless, low-stakes but large-scale action sequences, [director Jaume Collet-Serra] flies his horror flag by inserting cleverly staged creature scares, boosting a ride that would otherwise be a quiet commute.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise's Disneyfied sense of adventure never truly ignites.
reviews.author: Matt Conway

reviews.text: By all means enjoy yourself - but I would measure your expectations.
reviews.author: Grant Watson

reviews.text: Johnson and Blunt are enough to overcome the deficiencies, but with a stronger second act it could have been one of the year's more enjoyable rides.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise is at its best when Johnson and Blunt square off. The chemistry's there and both embrace the absurd while never winking at the audience.
reviews.author: Rebecca Murray

reviews.text: It becomes a bit long and grating, but the fun banter between Blunt and Johnson make the movie worth watching...kids by the way, will love it.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: In fifty years, Indiana Jones and Jack Sparrow will still be icons of imagination. Jungle Cruise will be a theme park tie-in that few can find and fewer will care to.
reviews.author: Ian Simmons

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise is an entertaining ride even if it sails on choppy waters at times.
reviews.author: Courtney Small

reviews.text: Ms. Blunt seems to be having fun playing a distaff version of Indiana Jones. Mr. Johnson is always the same, but being able to be yourself is exactly what separates mere movie actors from movie stars.
reviews.author: John Anderson

reviews.text: A rollicking adventure that captures the spirit of Indiana Jones! Emily Blunt provides the muscle, and Dwayne Johnson the laughs.
reviews.author: Joe Friar

reviews.text: The latest adaptation of yet another Disney attraction could've used more Jesse Plemons, but you could say that about most major movie releases. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mario Alegre

reviews.text: About as enjoyable as the ride itself. Which isn't saying all that much.
reviews.author: Jon Negroni

reviews.text: It's a wonderful summer movie, full of light and color and the great outdoors, with a sunny, winning attitude, brisk movement, and a lighthearted tone. What keeps it from being great is, perhaps, the lack of a certain looseness, or a freedom to frolic.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: Feels like watching complete The Mummy trilogy; starts off fantastic, then gets over the top but still funny, and eventually ends up forgetting what made it special to begin with, while blasting its protagonist with a CGI storm [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Rivera Rubio

reviews.text: Johnson and Blunt... make the most unexpectedly appealing screen couple of the year.
reviews.author: Ed Potton

reviews.text: Blunt and Johnson possess a natural, witty repartee. Even when they are at odds, which is often, their connection can still be felt.
reviews.author: George M. Thomas

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise is a cheeky, frolicky, fun movie voyage well worth taking! Stars Dwayne Johnson and Emily Blunt are off the charts charismatic, clever and entertaining!
reviews.author: Leah Sydney

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise is an extremely busy movie, but its perpetual motion means it rarely pauses to gaze upon its digital panoramas, nor to let its actors savour anything beyond their mostly undercooked repartee.
reviews.author: Luke Goodsell

reviews.text: The irresistibly charming stars help make this adventurous, occasionally swashbuckling ride adaptation amusing, if not as memorable as The Mummy or Pirates of the Caribbean.
reviews.author: Sandie Angulo Chen

reviews.text: While it might not return with previously unseen treasures, what it does rummage up pairs perfectly with a large bucket of popcorn and a slushy drink.
reviews.author: Karen Han

reviews.text: The brilliant cast, expertly steered by Dwayne Johnson and Emily Blunt, work overtime to save Jungle Cruise from wading into murky waters.
reviews.author: Sarah McIntyre

reviews.text: One strains to track what exactly is happening and why they ought to be invested in it.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: Despite the millions and millions of dollars worth of special effects on display in virtually every scene, the film simply never quite manages to conjure up any genuine moviegoing magic of its own.
reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: This Ride Should have Stayed in the Park
reviews.author: Kathia Woods

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise does evoke classic adventure films, but only in that you would rather be watching them than drifting along with this.
reviews.author: Jonathan Roberts

reviews.text: Plays like fan fiction for, like, all the Pirates of the Caribbean movies combined...If you're tempted to go easy on the slipshod plot, just recall what a well-oiled machine the original Pirates is.
reviews.author: Steven D. Greydanus

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise may boast two charismatic stars but it is a tiresome cocktail of cliches, occasionally good dad jokes, and borrowing from previous better films.
reviews.author: Lewis Knight

reviews.text: These movies-based-on-Disneyland-attractions are cash-grabby brand extensions that feel cynical the moment they're announced, so hold onto your hat. "Jungle Cruise" is pretty fun.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: The promising screwball comedy between its two main stars is drowned out by what feels like just another Pirates installment.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: While the film can ape the attire and the attitude of [Indiana Jones], it can't manage the rich sense of place that makes the earlier films classics.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: Like many Cruise vacations, Jungle Cruise will have you excited the first few days at sea, and then longing to quickly return to port.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: With its big budget on screen and numerous winking references to the original ride, I can only be so underwhelmed by the faults I have.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: [Jungle Cruise has] plenty of swashbuckling charm and loaded spectacle to soak up - maybe even guide the vessel away from the rockier bits.
reviews.author: Nguyên Lê

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise makes its aims and its inspirations apparent, but ultimately, it's just a model of -- as in, not real -- fun.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: [Jungle Cruise is ]a lifeless alleged spectacle filled with manufactured nature, celebrities, and bad puns that you'll forget the second it's over.
reviews.author: Matt Lynch

reviews.text: The queue line for the Jungle Cruise in Disneyland is more exciting.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise is a somewhat entertaining, though entirely derivative, adventure. It's nothing audiences haven't seen countless times before but at least the smorgasbord of eye-wateringly bad puns provides a touch of creativity.
reviews.author: Andrew Murray

reviews.text: A surprisingly fun adventure film full of charm, wit and genuine excitement.
reviews.author: Rob Dean

reviews.text: Strewn with A+ production values, Disney's latest four-quadrant crowd pleaser has the distinction of boasting a triad of refreshing, funny, even touching lead performances... Emily Blunt is so comically adroit here it comes as a something of a shock.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: No matter how appealing the leads, the set pieces are so generic and numerous they become like wallpaper.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: The movie can't sit still yet it never gets going.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: Disney's latest ride-into-movie adaption is high-spirited fun aimed squarely at kids.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: Like Vogon poetry, the plot of Disney's "Jungle Cruise" is mostly unintelligible and wants to beat you into submission.
reviews.author: Jeannette Catsoulis

reviews.text: It may not be another Pirates of the Caribbean but it exists as a reminder that inspiration can come from unusual places.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: There's some dodgy CGI and a slightly over-inflated running time but Jungle Cruise is much more fun than you might imagine a movie based on a theme park ride will be.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: A pleasant and fun diversion for the whole family that remains afloat with its wit and charm.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: "Jungle Cruise" is the ride to take - especially during these trying, turbulent times - this year
reviews.author: Caffeinated Clint

reviews.text: Even those addicted to this sort of theme-park-on-steroids-style mayhem may conclude that this 'Cruise' offers too much of it.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: [Collet-Serra] does what he can-and it is fun-but there's a better film still locked inside.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: Johnson and Blunt do have great chemistry together, but it's their individual affability that makes everything work so well.
reviews.author: Catherine Springer

reviews.text: Maybe it's too much to expect greatness from an adaptation that starts from a 20-minute theme park ride, but if (Disney) is going to go there, then it needs to do better.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: JUNGLE CRUISE does have its moments of great fun and hilarity.
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text: Johnson and Blunt are a terrific comic team -- they make it look so easy.
reviews.author: David Kaplan

reviews.text: Blub, blub.Even with this relatively benign ambition and an admittedly top-flight cast, the jungle's a bungle.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: It settles for being a lark, and its winning cast nails the frivolous good time it aims to be.
reviews.author: Emily Wheeler

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise works because Blunt and Johnson are a dream team.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise may be a fun ride at Disney parks, but as a movie it's stuck in the bog.
reviews.author: Alan Cerny

reviews.text: It seems rather coldly engineered, but that doesn't mean the result is without charm. In fact, it's packed with it. A huge part of the reason Jungle Cruise clips along cheerfully is the perfect casting of Emily Blunt and Dwayne Johnson.
reviews.author: Olly Richards

reviews.text: There's even an effervescent romantic comedy aspect to Disney's new theme-park-based fantasy/adventure.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: I wasn't completely won over by the film's second half which goes over to fantasy with a new cast of CGI creations but it's done with a lot of verve and wit and Johnson and Blunt still manage to keep a straight face.
reviews.author: Sandra Hall

reviews.text: So while "Jungle Cruise" isn't the worst ride you could take, it's probably a better move to just get back in line for Space Mountain again.
reviews.author: Mathew DeKinder

reviews.text: Johnson usually has enough charm to pull the audience through. But sometimes, he's not even enough of a presence to save a movie.
reviews.author: Max Covill

reviews.text: At Disneyland it may be smooth sailing, but on screen, "Jungle Cruise" proves a rocky ride.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise is an adventure that rarely feels truly exciting, which is never a good sign. While the film won't be the worst thing to show up on screens in 2021, it never lives up to its potential with two A-list actors leading the way.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: This is a much funnier, more buoyant movie than you might expect.
reviews.author: Leslie Felperin

reviews.text: If you don't fall asleep, there's plenty to look at...
reviews.author: Rex Reed

reviews.text: When push comes to shove, Jungle Cruise has all the right pieces in place where it counts -- it's a well-paced adventure flick with a duo of compelling leads.
reviews.author: Lauren Coates

reviews.text: There might be some expectation for seasoned B-director Jaume Collet-Serra to really bring something to the table in his official ascension to the big leagues, but he acts here as a more capable and efficient Jon Turteltaub.
reviews.author: Ethan Vestby

reviews.text: Great cast chemistry and a surprisingly clever plot twist elevates Jungle Cruise from the standard summer CGI spectacle. The film has no down beats over its swift two hour runtime.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: Despite some lackluster CGI, the charm of both leads is felt throughout this family adventure.
reviews.author: Yolanda Machado

reviews.text: [Updates] the adventurer genre. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Daniel de Partearroyo

reviews.text: Goes overboard.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: The first half is a terrific throwback to the days of high adventure, but the second half is over-the-top with a lame second half reveal.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise is non-stop fun from beginning to end.
reviews.author: Callum Crumlish

reviews.text: It's a first-class production of an empty concept and an utterly dead script.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: The trouble with a movie like "Jungle Cruise" is the comparison it invites. And in this case, the ride is better.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: I've dropped the phrase "live action cartoon" a fair bit in my time, but it's rarely been more appropriate than here - the whole exercise feels weightless and flimsy.
reviews.author: Travis Johnson

reviews.text: Overstuffed with generic villains and too rambling for its own good, Jungle Cruise offers nothing new or exciting ... It's a bland misfire that borrows heavily from Raiders of the Lost Ark and The African Queen. Jungle Cruise is more like Jungle Snooze.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: Full of fun, with another winning performance by Dwayne Johnson - I think if he met me he and I would be best pals immediately - "Jungle Cruise" is the latest Disney attraction to become a feature film and, I must say, it's pretty darn entertaining.
reviews.author: Michael A. Smith

reviews.text: There's some looseness to the picture early on, but the whole thing becomes unwieldy in a hurry, much like a "Pirates of the Caribbean" sequel.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: The two stars' big hearts bring a human element to this whirling apparatus. The film can sometimes feel more like a slog than a cruise, but Johnson and Blunt prove to be excellent company on the journey.
reviews.author: Tim Grierson

reviews.text: ... all audiences really want from a film like Jungle Cruise is a good time, which it delivers on all fronts. You'll laugh, you'll groan, and you may even hold your breath in anticipation as Collet-Serra takes us on a fantastical adventure ...
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise is a summer ride that will have you yearning for a theme park day-out once more.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: The very definition of a summer movie, it goes down easy with a large bucket of buttery popcorn and sugary soda, engaging from the first frame to the last.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: 'Jungle Cruise' is a movie that never met a cliché it didn't like.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: Stop the ride. I want to get off.
reviews.author: Dan Scully

reviews.text: A lightweight, lightly entertaining Disney flick for the entire family.
reviews.author: Richard Propes

reviews.text: You'll be hard pressed to find a more likeable duo than [Dwayne] Johnson and [Emily] Blunt, whose chemistry is as tropical, if not more so, than the sweltering jungle setting.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: It is hard for me to express just how difficult and dubious a feat it is to give me Johnson and Blunt and leave me wanting...less.
reviews.author: Kenneth R. Morefield

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise very much succeeds in bringing the ride to the big screen, while giving us a great story on top.
reviews.author: Jordy Sirkin

reviews.text: Like The Mummy before it, it's not without its flaws - but it knows how to have a good time.
reviews.author: Alex Cranz

reviews.text: There's no denying that Jungle Cruise is a rocky journey always on the verge of washing up ashore, but Blunt and Johnson are so great together you'll be aboard for the long haul.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: Dwayne Johnson is one of the most charismatic human beings on the planet, and Emily Blunt is also carrying her own weight here, but they can only do so much for Jungle Cruise with flimsy writing and mostly expressionless directing
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: While it often captures the high-spirited fun spirit of the first "Pirates" film, it also comes across as an inferior copy.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: Nice celebration of the Disney attraction. Like the skippers on the ride, Johnson tells very funny "bad jokes" & has great chemistry with Blunt. A few flaws but a lot of fun!
reviews.author: Grace Randolph

reviews.text: The chapeau in question is certainly stylish and attention-getting, but the head underneath doesn't quite have the full bluster to fit the look the hat and definition of "swashbuckler" call for.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: While "Jungle Cruise" wants to remind you of those classic adventure romance films, unfortunately, that's all it is, a reminder that those other films have vastly more emotional weight.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: Feels like a slick piece of corporate entertainment and not much else. I'm sure this movie's going to thrill and excite a lot of people. I'm just not one of them.
reviews.author: Dan Murrell

reviews.text: The experience the film more accurately simulates is the standing in line: all that tedious waiting in the heat for the fun to start.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: I have to give Disney credit for making Jungle Cruise the movie as close to riding Jungle Cruise, the theme park ride, as humanly possible. Just don't stand in too long a line for it.
reviews.author: Sarah Hagi

reviews.text: Jaume Collet-Serra's Amazonian adventure certainly goes all out to entertain. Yet it also reaches a point where it becomes exhausting.
reviews.author: Neil Smith

reviews.text: It may not be the most thrilling experience, but it sure goes down easy.
reviews.author: Clint Worthington

reviews.text: With the supernatural fantasy elements, it appears more and more like a derivation of the Pirates of the Caribbean franchise; how fitting, since that is also based on a ride.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise is a family fun adeventure that gives us the escapism we love when going to the movies.
reviews.author: Sharronda Williams

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise somewhat feels like Indiana Jones meets Pirates , but Johnson's confidence and Blunt's charisma allows it to stand on its own -- families will have a great time with this adventure
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise could have been hit or miss but thankfully, Disney did it right and the result is and fun, summer film.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: It doesn't overstay its welcome at a solid two hours, though it does go overboard by the end.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: a light, enjoyable romp through the jungle
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: A majestic action-adventure that keeps you amped up with its quick-paced action and a perpetually entertaining sense of humor.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: Once departing, there's no turning back from a bloated two hours, a convoluted story, goony wooden characters, and endless action that feels weightless.
reviews.author: Jason Escamilla

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise does what it needs to do in providing thrilling entertainment as a throwback feature while simultaneously making fans of the Disney attraction happy.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: The "Jungle Cruise" has so much CGI that you'd think it was the gaudy resurrection of a beloved Disney animated classic.
reviews.author: Nick Allen

reviews.text: Putting [Dwayne Johnson] in this role makes about as much sense as putting Pee-Wee Herman in a weight-lifting contest. Johnson is very, very good at what he does. But for the sake of all of us Rock fans, please: Don't ask the man to act.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: 'Jungle Cruise' is a delightful adventure that flies by thanks to oodles of charm up-and-down the cast-in Jaume Collet-Serra we forever trust, like we should.
reviews.author: Matt Donato

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise delivers about as ably as it possibly could, creating a light-hearted adventure that owes as much to The Mummy as anything in Disney's fleet.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: A rollicking adventure powered by invigorating camerawork and the hugely charming dynamic between Dwayne Johnson, Emily Blunt and Jack Whitehall.
reviews.author: Perri Nemiroff

reviews.text: A lifeless amalgamation of bits borrowed from better movies.
reviews.author: Evan Dossey

reviews.text: Yes, sometimes Jungle Cruise feels like it's going on for Niles and Niles. But it's a fun ride for the whole family! And if you don't believe me, you're in...disbelief.
reviews.author: Tania Lamb

reviews.text: In the pantheon of Disney movies based on Disney theme park rides, Jungle Cruise is pretty good -- leagues better than dreck like Haunted Mansion though not quite as satisfying as the original Pirates of the Caribbean.
reviews.author: Matt Zoller Seitz

reviews.text: Timid and neutered, it works so hard trying to remind you of 'Pirates of the Caribbean,' 'Romancing the Stone' and 'The Mummy' that it never affirms its own identity.
reviews.author: Scott Mendelson

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise provides a pulpy adventure that delights and entertains throughout.
reviews.author: Sean Mulvihill

reviews.text: Dwayne Johnson and Emily Blunt smolder and charm their way through an exotic adventure for all-ages. This stays true even when their characters' journey hits choppy waters.
reviews.author: David Crow

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise proves that the treasure hunting adventure formula still works. It's fun, it's audacious, and it's truly an experience that will bring joy to any age in the audience.
reviews.author: Kate Sánchez

reviews.text: A pleasure cruise and a thrill ride, all rolled into one perfect package!
reviews.author: Caitlin Kennedy

reviews.text: Action-adventure films like this are rare; a good one is even rarer. But this comes together for a fun and enjoyable family film.
reviews.author: EJ Moreno

reviews.text: The old world charm gets bogged down with fantastical CGI nonsense involving magic petals and immortal conquistadors. Please, someone cast Johnson in a movie for grown-ups.
reviews.author: Jack Hawkins

reviews.text: Credit goes only to its two stars that this is watchable, because the film is a derivative hodge-podge unworthy of their charisma. Just rewatch The Mummy and cut out the middle man.
reviews.author: Helen O'Hara

reviews.text: Like the ride itself, it requires no more mental engagement than you would devote to any theme park visit (excluding the thrill rides, which actually raise a pulse.)
reviews.author: Michael O'Sullivan

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise will remind you of a lot of things, but mostly it just feels like a classic Disney adventure tale. There's action, comedy, and even emotion.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: While Jungle Cruise may not be quite as modern as it sets out to be, it certainly isn't slacking when it comes to good, old-fashioned entertainment.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: It may fall well short of the lightning-in-a-bottle success enjoyed by the original Pirates, but it's an enjoyable escape into the wilds of the Amazon -- even if the CG animals are less convincing than their decades-old theme park counterparts.
reviews.author: Brent Hankins

reviews.text: While its overreliance on bombastic (and occasionally ghastly) CGI teeters on excessive, the sparkling chemistry of its two leads and a wonderfully exciting narrative make this one of the best thrill rides this season.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: Mostly it is up to Johnson and Blunt to make it work as they battle forces against them, as well as the overly busy special effects. The kids will eat it up.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: One can make it from the opening scene to the credits without the feeling that what they're watching is not a complete and satisfying film, but a cleverly packaged trailer for an as-yet-undeveloped sequel no one even had the opportunity to ask for.
reviews.author: Dominic Griffin

reviews.text: It's the gloriously bombastic, throwback blockbuster we've been missing for years and the most fun you'll have at the movies all summer.
reviews.author: Courtney Howard

reviews.text: "Jungle Cruise," despite its more-than-capable leads and its much-vaunted attention to detail and verisimilitude, never feels transporting in the way that even mediocre blockbusters were once able to muster.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: Some might enjoy meandering down Jungle Cruise's lazy river, but most will realize they're simply marinating in recycled juices.
reviews.author: Jacob Oller

reviews.text: Compared to other attempts to turn theme park attractions into fresh revenue streams, it's not as lifeless as The Haunted Mansion or Tomorrowland. But that doesn't mean it's good.
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: The filmmakers should've just taken the same approach I use at a sushi buffet. Less is more.
reviews.author: Joey Morona

reviews.text: The film splutters out into something directionless and derivative and dull.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: Not since Aguirre has a trek into the Amazon felt quite so hamstrung by delusions of grandeur. Perhaps Disney's remake of "Fitzcarraldo" will fare better.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: Joyful family entertainment that'll keep naughty parents amused too.
reviews.author: Lou Thomas

reviews.text: Like a zanier Bogie and Bacall, Johnson and Blunt cross an "African Queen" vibe with Indiana Jones flair for a period piece that starts like gangbusters but can't keep from wading into familiar waters.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: JUNGLE CRUISE is great fun, but it does hit some bumps along its journey.
reviews.author: Sarah Musnicky

reviews.text: For all its limitations, it will probably do the job for families - after all, it's unlikely many seven-year-olds will share my disappointment with the slapdash sound mix or muddy grading.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: Jaume Collet-Serra's deft touches elevate what otherwise feels like another formulaic contemporary Disney blockbuster.
reviews.author: Jake Cole

reviews.text: ...after development hell, years of delay, and a global pandemic, Jungle Cruise has finally set sail for the big screen, and it's an absolute waste of time.
reviews.author: Ryan McQuade

reviews.text: We're not here to break the mold. We're here to re-familiarize ourselves with the concept of molds.
reviews.author: William Bibbiani

reviews.text: "Jungle Cruise" is a movie that implicitly asks: What's wrong with a little good old-fashioned escapism? The answer is: Absolutely nothing...
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: What is great about 'Jungle Cruise' is that it doesn't take itself too seriously. It knows it's a movie based on a beloved ride. The action is good, the acting is good. It won't win awards, but it will win the hearts of many from young to old.
reviews.author: Catalina Combs

reviews.text: Emily Blunt and Dwayne Johnson are the movie's true treasure. (...) A perfect film for all the family to enjoy on the big screen. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jesus Agudo

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise is a joyous summer romp rooted on by a fun script and some completely captivating chemistry between stars Johnson and Blunt.
reviews.author: Matt Fowler

reviews.text: A PUN-FILLED adventure that captures the heart of the ride while giving viewers an incredible and surprising story. Incredible cast chemistry makes this one a blast!
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: An action-packed adventure full of heart, Jungle Cruise is the perfect Summer blockbuster for the whole family.
reviews.author: Nicola Austin

reviews.text: Almost willfully awful at times, but it's so good-natured and witty that you overcome the head-shakes and eye-rolling to realize you're having fun.
reviews.author: Phil Villarreal

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise is the adventure we've been waiting for, the kind of grand tale that reminds us of the movies that made many of us love movies in the first place.
reviews.author: Charlie Ridgely

reviews.text: Led by the delightful pairing of Emily Blunt and Dwayne Johnson, ﻿Jungle Cruise﻿ knows how to enjoy itself, even if the journey is a bit overstuffed.
reviews.author: Rachel LaBonte

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise is a really big fun movie and I think the first one we've had in a while that isn't part of another franchise. It's just a good time for two hours to sit back and enjoy this summer.
reviews.author: Julian Lytle

reviews.text: Everyone knows that your skipper makes or breaks your Jungle Cruise ride experience. Even though I had my doubts, Dwayne Johnson doesn't disappoint.
reviews.author: Christie Cronan

reviews.text: 'Jungle Cruise' chugs along its course, offering thrills and spills, annoyingly funny puns, absolutely zero chemistry between its leads, an extended cameo by a scoundrelous Paul Giamatti, and complete disregard for physics.
reviews.author: Brian Lloyd

reviews.text: Jungle Cruise is a ride you won't want to get off; with its charming three leads and a standout villain in Jesse Plemons, you'll be all aboard (sorry) for a fun family blockbuster that reminds us why we love going to the movies.
reviews.author: Josh Wilding

reviews.text: Dwayne Johnson and Emily Blunt share amazing chemistry in an adventure like we haven't had in a long while.
reviews.author: Leigh Monson

reviews.text: (It's) filled the PIRATES sized hole in my life... A good old fashioned fun and exciting pulpy romp, with charismatic leads and electric high fantasy action adventure, that fits right alongside the classic Disney adventures we all grew up with!
reviews.author: Dave Lee

synopsis: Join fan favorites Dwayne Johnson and Emily Blunt for the adventure of a lifetime on Disney's JUNGLE CRUISE, a rollicking thrill-ride down the Amazon with wisecracking skipper Frank Wolff and intrepid researcher Dr. Lily Houghton. Lily travels from London, England to the Amazon jungle and enlists Frank's questionable services to guide her downriver on La Quila--his ramshackle-but-charming boat. Lily is determined to uncover an ancient tree with unparalleled healing abilities--possessing the power to change the future of medicine. Thrust on this epic quest together, the unlikely duo encounters innumerable dangers and supernatural forces, all lurking in the deceptive beauty of the lush rainforest. But as the secrets of the lost tree unfold, the stakes reach even higher for Lily and Frank and their fate--and mankind's--hangs in the balance.
